result.rule: Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.

Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Compare the model with the description; remove unsupported elements and retain every explicitly stated alternative, outcome and collaboration.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Use transaction, ad-hoc or compensation behavior only when its specific semantics are explicitly described.

args.text: When a description presents alternative outcomes as the result or content of one action, without describing distinct follow-up activities or routing, model the action without inventing separate activities or a gateway to represent those outcomes.

trace.reason: Check whether an existing learned guideline already covers this modeling choice.

result.rule: When the description specifies a follow-up for one outcome of a decision but does not state what happens for the alternative outcome: Model the stated outcome and its follow-up, but do not invent a separate activity or end event for the unspecified alternative.

When the description states that a participant may perform one of several alternative actions: Model each stated action as an activity on its corresponding decision branch; do not represent the actions only as alternative end events.

When the description states that a condition leads to a distinct activity or to ending the case: Model each stated outcome on its corresponding branch, connecting it to the required activity or end; do not omit the activity or leave the outcome without a modeled destination.

When the description presents multiple activities that can follow the same preceding activity and does not specify an order between them: Model the activities as parallel branches using a parallel gateway.
